content:
Facts: 
The Ne Zha film series animation director is Jiao Zi (stage name), whose real name is Yang Yu.  He attended  West China School of Pharmacy, Sichuan University.  In year three at the university, Jiao Zi stared to self-learn animation after finding he was not interested in pharmacy.  After graduation, he decided to stay at home to develop animation films. His mother supported him and persuaded his father to stand with their son’s decision.  During this period, Jiao Zi’s father passed away. His break came in 2009 when a 16 minute long animated short film by him won numerous domestic and international awards. He later stared his own studio produced several works including the Ne Zha series.  If his dad is alive, would be very proud of him now and his mom too.  💕👍

author: @linglingchong7198
content:
I got to know Ne Zha by accident, this movie was introduced to me by my dad because it was sensational in mainland China, and even Elon Musk posted about it. At first, I was skeptical, weighed down by the stereotype that Chinese animation couldn't match up to global standards. In fact, I was reluctant to watch it at all. But when my dad; an avid supporter of The Land of the Dragon insisted, I gave in and bought the tickets online.  

Determined not to watch a sequel without context, I looked up Ne Zha 1 a few days prior. To my surprise, it was incredible. The film shattered every preconceived notion I had about Ne Zha as a god or legendary figure. This version of Ne Zha was raw, rebellious, and compelling. His final words, "I determine my own fate," echoed in my mind long after the credits rolled.  

So there I was, in the cinema for Ne Zha 2, expecting a decent continuation. What I got instead was an exhilarating experience that had me laughing, gasping, and fully immersed. The storytelling was gripping, the character development was heartfelt, and the plot twists were top-notch.  

What I loved most was Ne Zha’s evolution, not just as a warrior but as a person. He was no longer just a lonely boy; he had forged meaningful bonds with Ao Bing, Si Fu, and the pig. His relationship with his father had improved, and his mother remained his unwavering pillar of love.  

To China, you deserve all the hype. Keep pushing boundaries and breaking records because Ne Zha 2 proves that Chinese animation is a force to be reckoned with. Highly recommended!
